decision_description: Phase 2 Concept Refinement has confirmed that the MAESTRO project concept is substantively aligned with the HORIZON-CL4-2026-05-DIGITAL-EMERGING-02 call scope. Both expected outcomes are mapped and confirmed: EO-01 (significant improvements in AI agent autonomy, robustness, and reliability through advanced planning, memory management, and reasoning) is addressed by Pillar 1 (Neuro-Symbolic Planning and Reasoning), Pillar 2 (Adaptive Memory Architecture), and the External Tool and API Orchestration Layer, with vocabulary gap 'planning mechanisms' identified for adoption in proposal text. EO-02 (innovative multi-agent frameworks demonstrating effective decentralised coordination and collaboration beyond individual agent capabilities) is addressed by Pillar 3 (Decentralised Multi-Agent Coordination) and the External Tool and API Orchestration Layer, with vocabulary gap 'multi-agent frameworks' identified for adoption. All six mandatory scope requirements (SR-01 through SR-06) are confirmed covered. Three partially covered non-mandatory items require proposal text action: CC-01 (TRL 2 start-level must be explicitly declared in proposal text; TRL 5 end-point is confirmed but TRL 2 origin is absent from concept documents), CC-03 (prior EU-funded actions to be explicitly identified and cited as build-upon basis), CC-13 (synergies with named national, regional, and international initiatives beyond EU-level partnerships to be stated). Four eligibility and portfolio items remain for resolution in later phases: CC-09 and CC-10 (geographic eligibility and control structure for all 8 consortium partners pending full consortium data population in Tier 3), CC-11 (MAESTRO targets healthcare and advanced manufacturing portfolio slots; WP8 architectural mapping analysis addresses in-vehicle autonomous driving transferability but does not constitute a validated sector demonstrator and does not fill the in-vehicle autonomous driving portfolio coverage slot), CC-12 (FSTP applicability and allocation not addressed in concept; must be resolved during budget phase). Two Phase 1 scope flags (logistics and supply chain demonstrator framing relative to Apply AI portfolio sectors; in-vehicle autonomous driving portfolio slot positioning) require explicit proposal text treatment to prevent evaluator ambiguity. A reference numbering mismatch between concept document SR-XX and CC-XX identifiers and the Tier 2B extraction identifiers must be reconciled before proposal finalisation to ensure cross-references are evaluator-verifiable. Vocabulary alignment and strategic differentiation narrative confirmed as consistent with call scope and sufficient for Phase 2 gate passage.
alternatives_considered: Declare concept alignment failed or partial due to partially covered items — rejected because all mandatory scope requirements (SR-01 through SR-06) are confirmed covered; partially covered items are non-mandatory expectations or eligibility data gaps addressable in later phases without undermining the concept's fundamental alignment with the call's substantive research scope.

Record only confirmed-covered items and defer gap and flag documentation to Phase 8 drafting — rejected as incompatible with CLAUDE.md §9.4, which requires durable decision records at decision time, not deferred to agent memory, and with CLAUDE.md §12.1, which requires phase outputs to identify inferences, assumptions, and flags for reviewability.

Treat vocabulary gaps ('planning mechanisms', 'multi-agent frameworks') as scope misalignments requiring concept revision — rejected because these are terminology alignment items, not substantive scope conflicts; the underlying research activities directly address the call vocabulary and the gaps are minor adoptions for proposal text, not architectural changes.
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §7 — Phase 2: Concept Refinement gate condition (topic mapping confirmed; concept note vocabulary aligned with call-specific expected outcomes; strategic positioning identifies differentiation within call scope; scope_conflict_log is empty, confirming no unresolved scope conflicts); Tier 2B docs/tier2b_topic_and_call_sources/extracted/expected_outcomes.json (EO-01, EO-02 mapping sources); Tier 2B docs/tier2b_topic_and_call_sources/extracted/scope_requirements.json (SR-01 through SR-14 coverage sources); Tier 2B docs/tier2b_topic_and_call_sources/extracted/call_constraints.json (CC-01 through CC-13 coverage sources)
rationale: The Phase 2 gate condition under CLAUDE.md §7 requires confirmation of four conditions before the gate is satisfied: (1) topic mapping is confirmed; (2) concept note vocabulary is aligned with call-specific expected outcomes; (3) strategic positioning identifies the proposal's differentiation within the call scope; and (4) no unresolved scope conflicts remain between the concept and Tier 2B. All four conditions are met as evidenced by the phase outputs. Topic mapping is confirmed in docs/tier3_project_instantiation/call_binding/topic_mapping.json with explicit Tier 2B and Tier 3 source references for both EO-01 and EO-02. Vocabulary alignment is confirmed with two minor vocabulary gaps identified for adoption in proposal text, which are terminology items rather than substantive conflicts. Strategic differentiation is documented in full in concept_refinement_summary.json identifying the integrated three-pillar architecture unified by the External Tool and API Orchestration Layer as the primary differentiator against three distinct existing research communities. The scope_conflict_log in concept_refinement_summary.json is empty, confirming no unresolved scope conflicts exist. Partially covered items and flagged scope items are appropriately classified as follow-up actions and risk items, not as scope conflicts, because they concern non-mandatory expectations, pending data from later phases, or framing choices for proposal text — none of them contradict the concept's alignment with the call's substantive AI agent research scope. The concept alignment decision is therefore resolved at the Phase 2 gate. Durable recording is required per CLAUDE.md §9.4 and §13.5 to ensure this determination is not held only in agent memory.
